title: UCCX Real-Time Queue and Agent Monitoring
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'UCCX Real-Time Queue and Agent Monitoring' only. Does not supplant cross-domain SIEM playbooks for unrelated domains or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `operational_exceptions.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `operations_uccx_real_time_queue_and_agent_monitoring` (UC-11.3.45), SOC dashboard panel "Operations — UCCX Real-Time Queue and Agent Monitoring", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:ops_controls.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=contact_center` sourcetype='uccx:csq_stats' where `csq_name` satisfies `avail_agents` > 0 for UC-11.3.45 ('UCCX Real-Time Queue and Agent Monitoring'). Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `contact_center` / `uccx:csq_stats` events where `csq_name` stays below `avail_agents` > 0, or exclude the test entity via `ops_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-11.3.45.

dataSources: `sourcetype=uccx:csq_stats` (custom via REST API), `sourcetype=uccx:agent_stats`, UCCX wallboard XML feed Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
app: Custom scripted input (UCCX REST API / Finesse API), `Splunk Connect for Syslog` — Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617)
spl:
index=contact_center sourcetype="uccx:csq_stats"
| stats latest(calls_waiting) as waiting, latest(calls_handled) as handled, latest(calls_abandoned) as abandoned, latest(longest_wait_sec) as longest_wait, latest(agents_available) as avail_agents by csq_name
| eval calls_per_agent=if(avail_agents>0, round(waiting/avail_agents, 1), "N/A - No Agents")
| eval alert_level=case(
    waiting>10 AND avail_agents==0, "CRITICAL",
    waiting>5 OR longest_wait>120, "WARNING",
    1==1, "OK")
| table csq_name, waiting, handled, abandoned, longest_wait, avail_agents, calls_per_agent, alert_level
| sort -waiting
description: Cisco Unified Contact Center Express (UCCX) remains widely deployed for small-to-medium contact centers. Native UCCX reporting is limited to historical views, and Finesse supervisor gadgets show only a single queue at a time. Splunk aggregation of UCCX queue statistics provides a unified real-time and historical view across all Contact Service Queues (CSQs), enabling supervisors to spot developing queue emergencies and workforce planners to validate staffing models with actual data.
value: Early 'UCCX Real-Time Queue and Agent Monitoring' detection reduces operational risk and delayed incident response by giving Operations operators a Splunk-native signal before manual triage or audit channels surface the issue.
implementation: Deploy a scripted input that polls the UCCX REST API (available on port 9443) for CSQ statistics every 60 seconds. The API returns calls waiting, calls handled, calls abandoned, average/max wait times, and available agents per CSQ. Parse into structured events and index. For agent-level data, poll the Finesse REST API for agent state and call details. Alert when any CSQ has calls waiting with zero available agents (immediate customer impact). Provide a wallboard-style dashboard with auto-refresh for supervisors. Track historical queue performance trends to validate workforce management forecasts. Combine with UCCX Historical Reporting data for end-of-day analytics.
visualization: Single value tiles (calls waiting, longest wait, available agents — per CSQ), Table (all CSQs with status), Line chart (calls waiting trend over shift), Bar chart (handled vs abandoned by CSQ).
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable; primary SPL uses raw or vendor-normalized event fields.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `contact_center`** — Planned work for 'UCCX Real-Time Queue and Agent Monitoring' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `csq_name` remains in-scope for UC-11.3.45. Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `uccx:csq_stats`** — Scheduled automation elevates `calls_per_agent` without crossing `avail_agents` > 0. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `csq_name`** — Health checks in `contact_center` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `uccx:csq_stats`** — First 48h baseline for `csq_name` is unstable; window via `ops_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `ops_exception_register.csv` keyed on `csq_name`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.

Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Custom scripted input (UCCX REST API / Finesse API), `Splunk Connect for Syslog`.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `sourcetype=uccx:csq_stats` (custom via REST API), `sourcetype=uccx:agent_stats`, UCCX wallboard XML feed.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Deploy a scripted input that polls the UCCX REST API (available on port 9443) for CSQ statistics every 60 seconds. The API returns calls waiting, calls handled, calls abandoned, average/max wait times, and available agents per CSQ. Parse into structured events and index. For agent-level data, poll the Finesse REST API for agent state and call details. Alert when any CSQ has calls waiting with zero available agents (immediate customer impact). Provide a wallboard-style dashboard with auto-refresh…

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=contact_center sourcetype="uccx:csq_stats"
| stats latest(calls_waiting) as waiting, latest(calls_handled) as handled, latest(calls_abandoned) as abandoned, latest(longest_wait_sec) as longest_wait, latest(agents_available) as avail_agents by csq_name
| eval calls_per_agent=if(avail_agents>0, round(waiting/avail_agents, 1), "N/A - No Agents")
| eval alert_level=case(
    waiting>10 AND avail_agents==0, "CRITICAL",
    waiting>5 OR longest_wait>120, "WARNING",
    1==1, "OK")
| table csq_name, waiting, handled, abandoned, longest_wait, avail_agents, calls_per_agent, alert_level
| sort -waiting
```

Understanding this SPL

**UCCX Real-Time Queue and Agent Monitoring** — Cisco Unified Contact Center Express (UCCX) remains widely deployed for small-to-medium contact centers. Native UCCX reporting is limited to historical views, and Finesse supervisor gadgets show only a single queue at a time. Splunk aggregation of UCCX queue statistics provides a unified real-time and historical view across all Contact Service Queues (CSQs), enabling supervisors to spot developing queue emergencies and workforce planners to validate staffing models with…

Documented **Data sources**: `sourcetype=uccx:csq_stats` (custom via REST API), `sourcetype=uccx:agent_stats`, UCCX wallboard XML feed. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Custom scripted input (UCCX REST API / Finesse API), `Splunk Connect for Syslog`. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: contact_center; **sourcetype**: uccx:csq_stats. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=contact_center, sourcetype="uccx:csq_stats". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by csq_name** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **calls_per_agent** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• `eval` defines or adjusts **alert_level** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Pipeline stage (see **UCCX Real-Time Queue and Agent Monitoring**): table csq_name, waiting, handled, abandoned, longest_wait, avail_agents, calls_per_agent, alert_level
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.


Step 3 — Validate
Compare with call center wallboards, ACD/IVR config, and Webex contact center or UCCX real-time data for the same queue and time.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Single value tiles (calls waiting, longest wait, available agents — per CSQ), Table (all CSQs with status), Line chart (calls waiting trend over shift), Bar chart (handled vs abandoned by CSQ).

Scripted input (generic example)
This use case relies on a scripted input. In the app's local/inputs.conf add a stanza such as:

```ini
[script://$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/YourApp/bin/collect.sh]
interval = 300
sourcetype = your_sourcetype
index = main
disabled = 0
```

The script should print one event per line (e.g. key=value). Example minimal script (bash):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Output metrics or events, one per line
echo "metric=value timestamp=$(date +%s)"
```
